status: Died 2026-01-31 under Cal. Const. art. IV, sec. 10(c); filed with Chief Clerk pursuant to Joint Rule 56 on 2026-02-02
key_provisions: Would have expanded I-Bank financing eligibility for projects capturing and converting data center waste heat.

status: Passed Assembly; read second time and amended, re-referred to Senate Appropriations 2026-07-02 (hearing set 2026-08-03)
key_provisions: Would require monthly reporting to CEC on data center location, floor area, electrical capacity, water and energy consumption, PUE, WUE, onsite generation, generator fuel, procurement, and noise; local agencies would receive data at permitting stage.

status: Held under submission in Assembly Appropriations suspense file, 2026-05-14; no action since
key_provisions: Broader CEQA bill affecting industrial facilities near overburdened communities; would add notice, hearing, and translation duties and may affect data center siting in industrial areas.

status: Held under submission in Senate Appropriations (having passed the Assembly floor 2025-06-02, 57-18), 2025-08-29; no action since
key_provisions: Would require data center power usage effectiveness reporting and cost-shift assessment in energy planning.

status: Passed Assembly; read second time and amended, re-referred to Senate Appropriations 2026-07-02 (hearing set 2026-08-03)
key_provisions: Requires the CPUC to establish, by 2028-01-01, a separate electricity rate class/tariff for data centers so costs are proportional to cost-to-serve; requires large new data center transmission-level service agreements after 2027-01-01 to include minimum 10-year contract terms, prepayment of interconnection costs, and support for clean energy/wildfire mitigation programs; extends comparable requirements to CCAs and ESPs serving data centers.

status: Passed Assembly; read second time and amended, re-referred to Senate Appropriations 2026-07-02 (hearing set 2026-08-03)
key_provisions: Would revive and expand water-use reporting for data centers and require DWR/CEC guidance on water-efficient data center practices.

status: Vetoed by Governor 2025-10-11; consideration of veto stricken from file 2026-01-22
key_provisions: Would have required data center water-use estimates and annual water-use reporting tied to business licenses and permits.

status: Passed Senate 2026-05-27 (30-9); re-referred to Assembly Appropriations 2026-06-25 (hearing set 2026-08-05)
key_provisions: Requires the CPUC to establish data center rate structures ensuring data centers pay their reasonable share of transmission/distribution costs, contribute to clean energy procurement, and that rate design shields residential and low-income (CARE/FERA) customers from cost shifting.

status: Failed; from committee and from Assembly without further action, 2024-11-30 (prior 2023-2024 session concluded)
key_provisions: Proposed certification/exemption framework for certain thermal powerplants linked to data centers, including backup generation and air district review.

status: Chaptered by Secretary of State, Ch. 647, Statutes of 2025, 2025-10-11
key_provisions: Requires CPUC report to the Legislature by 2027-01-01 on whether new data center loads shift electrical costs to other customers; repeals 2031-01-01.

status: Passed Senate; read second time and amended, re-referred to Assembly Appropriations 2026-06-29 (hearing set 2026-08-05)
key_provisions: California Technology Innovation and Ratepayer Protection Act; would require CPUC tariff for participating data center customers, cost responsibility for transmission upgrades, early termination fees, clean-energy procurement, demand response participation, and no cost shifting to nonparticipating customers.

status: Passed Senate; read second time and amended, re-referred to Assembly Appropriations 2026-06-29 (hearing set 2026-08-05)
key_provisions: Would bar CEQA categorical exemptions for data center projects and allow qualifying data centers to seek environmental leadership development project streamlining if they meet conditions for energy, water, infrastructure costs, labor, and community benefits.

status: Held under submission in Senate Appropriations suspense file, 2026-05-14; no action since
key_provisions: Would regulate large-scale energy users/data centers through labor and electricity-rate provisions; LA County motion describes a separate energy rate class, clean backup generation, reporting, and local workforce requirements.
